## Why This Is Asked
Tests a designer’s ability to translate tenancy isolation into concrete IAM, storage structure, and CI validation using GCS features beyond high-level concepts.

## Key Concepts
- Storage schema decisions: per-tenant buckets vs prefixes; Uniform bucket-level access
- IAM Conditions and ABAC for tenant isolation
- Access patterns: signed URLs, short‑lived tokens
- Exfiltration controls: VPC Service Controls/Private Service Connect
- CI validation for synthetic tenants and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```json
{
  "bindings": [
    {
      "role": "roles/storage.objectViewer",
      "members": ["group:tenants@example.com"],
      "condition": {
        "title": "TenantIsolation",
        "description": "Access only to tenant prefix",
        "expression": "resource.name.startsWith('projects/_/buckets/tenant-bucket/objects/tenant-' + request.auth.claims['tid'] + '/')"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test for cross-tenant exfiltration in CI?
- How would you adapt if a tenant needs temporary cross-tenant analytics access?
